MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sex: Male
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Male fertility investigation

TEST PERFORMED
Y Chromosome Microdeletion Analysis by Multiplex PCR

METHODOLOGY
Multiplex PCR amplification was performed to detect microdeletions in the AZF (Azoospermia Factor) regions of the Y chromosome. The following sequence-tagged sites (STS) markers were analyzed:

• AZFa region: sY84, sY86
• AZFb region: sY127, sY134
• AZFc region: sY254, sY255
• Control markers: SRY (Yp11.31), Amelogenin X (Xp22.2), Amelogenin Y (Yp11.2)

DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. PCR amplification was performed using validated primer sets following EAA/EMQN best practice guidelines. Products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis.

RESULTS

MARKER		REGION		RESULT
sY84		AZFa		PRESENT
sY86		AZFa		PRESENT
sY127		AZFb		PRESENT
sY134		AZFb		PRESENT
sY254		AZFc		PRESENT
sY255		AZFc		PRESENT
SRY		Yp11.31		PRESENT
Amelogenin X	Xp22.2		PRESENT
Amelogenin Y	Yp11.2		PRESENT

INTERPRETATION
No complete AZFa, AZFb or AZFc deletions detected. All tested markers within the AZF regions are present.

TECHNICAL LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect complete deletions of AZFa, AZFb, and AZFc regions with a detection rate >95% for clinically significant AZF deletions. The test cannot detect:
• Small microdeletions within AZF regions that do not encompass the flanking marker sequences
• Deletions outside the AZF regions
• Point mutations or small insertions/deletions within genes
• Partial AZF deletions that retain the tested STS markers
• Mosaicism below the detection threshold of 20%

CLINICAL CORRELATION
No Y chromosome microdeletions were detected that would explain male infertility. Y chromosome microdeletions account for approximately 10-15% of cases of severe oligozoospermia and azoospermia. The absence of AZF deletions does not exclude other genetic or non-genetic causes of male infertility.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Refer to previous G-banded chromosome analysis for evaluation of chromosomal abnormalities
2. Consider additional genetic testing if clinically indicated, including:
   • Karyotype analysis if not previously performed
   • CFTR gene analysis for congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens
   • Hormonal evaluation including FSH, LH, and testosterone levels
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss results and reproductive options

REFERENCES
1. Krausz C, et al. EAA/EMQN best practice guidelines for molecular diagnosis of Y-chromosomal microdeletions. Andrology. 2014;2(1):5-19.
2. Colaco S, Modi D. Genetics of the human Y chromosome and its association with male infertility. Reprod Biol Endocrinol. 2018;16(1):14.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
